title: BSA Committee Meeting – July 10, 2026
transcript:
Wesley Tran: Okay, let's get started. It's two o'clock, we have all three committee members. Agenda today: one, the open alert on the high-risk member c_0086; two, BSAWatch tuning after last month's false positive spike; three, the quarterly training refresh; and four, anything for the examiner prep list. Chris, you've got the casework, so start us off.
Chris Burgess: Thanks, Wesley. So the case is {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0086}}, individual member, joined October of last year, one share savings account, {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00176}}. Risk rating is high. The alert came out of BSAWatch about two weeks ago. Pattern is a series of incoming ACH credits, each under $3,000, followed within a day or two by outbound wires-style activity going to a single counterparty, Glenn, Collins and Black, a Delaware business entity.
Monica Feld: And that's cp_015 in our counterparty table. I pulled the history. Since January there have been eleven incoming ACH credits, total about $27,400, and four outbound transfers totaling roughly $26,100. So the balance basically never builds. It's pass-through.
Wesley Tran: What's the stated purpose on the member file? Employment, business, what?
Chris Burgess: Onboarding says salaried employment and personal savings only. No business activity declared. That's the mismatch. The inbound originators are a mix, a couple of payment processors and some individuals. Nothing that looks like payroll.
Monica Feld: I'd also flag that the counterparty details came in through the member's outbound instructions. The beneficiary banking details on file, the {{CP_IBAN:cp_015}} and the {{CP_SWIFT:cp_015}}, were entered manually twice with slightly different formatting. Could be nothing, could be someone being careless, but I noted it.
Wesley Tran: Okay. Did we try contacting the member?
Chris Burgess: Zachary Powers is the member advocate and relationship owner. He called the number on file, {{CLIENT_PHONE:c_0086}}, twice, and left a voicemail. We also sent a secure message to {{CLIENT_EMAIL:c_0086}}. No response yet. I don't want to push too hard since we don't want to tip off anything if this ends up being a SAR.
Wesley Tran: Agreed. Let's not have Zachary discuss suspicion, just a routine account review outreach. Are we verifying identity data again? I want to be sure the profile is current.
Monica Feld: I ran the CIP refresh. The address of record, {{CLIENT_ADDRESS:c_0086}}, matches the last mailing that wasn't returned. The SSN on file, {{CLIENT_SSN:c_0086}}, passes verification, and the date of birth, {{CLIENT_DOB:c_0086}}, is consistent with the ID scanned at opening. So identity looks solid. It's the activity that concerns me, not the identity.
Wesley Tran: Good. Is there any chance the account is being used as a money mule account, with a third party controlling it?
Chris Burgess: That's my working theory. Quick ramp-up of inbound, immediate outbound, and the online login history shows access from several different devices in a short window. I'll ask IT through Andre Dubois's team for the MemberSSO login detail so we can look at that more closely.
Wesley Tran: Fine. What's your recommendation on timing?
Chris Burgess: Open a formal investigation now, keep the account open under enhanced monitoring for thirty days, and make the SAR decision at the next committee meeting unless something escalates. If the outbound pace increases, I'd come back to you for a restriction.
Wesley Tran: I'm okay with that. Decision: case stays open, enhanced monitoring, SAR decision on the August meeting, earlier if activity changes. Chris owns the case and the narrative draft. Monica, you handle the counterparty research on cp_015.
Monica Feld: Will do. I'll check the Delaware registry, adverse media, and whether other members have sent to that same entity.
Wesley Tran: Good. Now second item, BSAWatch tuning. Monica?
Monica Feld: So June we had around 140 alerts on the structuring scenario, and 118 were closed as false positives. A big chunk were members making regular deposits just under the threshold for legitimate reasons, like a small business doing weekly cash deposits. I'd like to propose raising the aggregation window on that rule from three days to five and adding a suppression for members with documented cash-intensive business profiles.
Chris Burgess: I'm a little wary of the suppression. That's exactly the profile that can hide structuring. Could we instead lower the priority rather than suppress?
Monica Feld: That works. Lower priority, still generates an alert, but routes to the second queue.
Wesley Tran: I prefer that. Don't suppress anything outright. Also, BSAWatch depends on CoreBanking and ACHHub, so any change needs to be tested when those feeds are stable. Monica, work with Hector Salas on a test environment run, and bring me the before and after alert counts.
Monica Feld: Understood. I'll aim for a result by July 24.
Wesley Tran: Third item, training. Chris?
Chris Burgess: The annual refresh is due by the end of September. I'd like to include a module on mule account typologies, using anonymized elements from this case, and a short one for tellers on recognizing third-party coaching at the window. Paul Jensen's team will need to schedule the floor staff.
Wesley Tran: Good, I'll email Paul about scheduling. Chris, draft the content outline by August 7.
Chris Burgess: Will do.
Wesley Tran: Last item, exam prep. The examiner list asks for our independent testing report and the risk assessment update. Monica, is the risk assessment current?
Monica Feld: Mostly. I still need to add the new ACH origination volumes from ACHHub. I can finish that by July 31.
Wesley Tran: Okay. Let me recap the action items. Chris, case ownership and narrative, SAR recommendation for August, plus the MemberSSO login request to Andre's team this week, and the training outline by August 7. Monica, cp_015 research, BSAWatch tuning test with Hector by July 24, and the risk assessment update by July 31. I'll talk to Paul about training logistics and tell Zachary to keep outreach routine. Anything else?
Chris Burgess: No, that covers it.
Monica Feld: Nothing from me.
Wesley Tran: Great. Thanks, everyone. We're adjourned.
